From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit pricing & technical fit (batching / kv cache / quantization)

Asha —

Great to meet you and the team. High-level answers below and I’ve attached a compact spreadsheet with commit-tier pricing and an appendix of technical notes. Long story short: there are three levers we commonly combine for the best unit economics:

1) Autoscale + reserved commit band: baseline savings, predictable throughput and preferred pricing
2) Optimize toolkit credits (one-time pilot credits or recurring optimizer credits) that apply against tokens saved via batching/cache; these can be used during PoC and ramp
3) Model quantization profile (4-bit BF16-int4 mixed paths) — this reduces GPU cost per token but requires a small MQE (model quality evaluation) sweep to ensure no customer-visible regressions

Short answers to your bullets:
- Pricing breakdown: see tab "Summary" in the attached. Example: for interactive LLM usage with 16k context, recommended starter: 6 month commit at $60k/mo (net effective 20% off list) + $12k one-time optimize toolkit advisory (includes quant sweep and ops runbook). Pilot credits can offset the first 2 months of token spend.
- Stacking discounts: commit band discounts are applied to hosted token rates; Optimize toolkit credits are separate line items and do not reduce list unit price but are applied as credits on the invoice. We can structure pilot credits to convert into a recurring discount if you convert to a reserve within 90 days.
- Performance tradeoffs: with continuous batching and KV prefix caching we typically maintain P95 response times in the 120–220ms range at 8–12k tokens/sec throughput on our dedicated pools. Quantization introduces some variance; our int4 execution path adds ~5–15ms per token in our benchmarks but reduces GPU cost by ~30–45% depending on model.

I’ve copied Priyom (commercial) and Karthik (inference lead) to help with the deal mechanics and the quant/ops plan.

Next step: if you’re OK, we’ll send back a short mutually actionable pricing path (pilot -> reserve) with a recommended set of technical acceptance tests.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit pricing & technical fit (batching / kv cache / quantization)

Asha —

Adding a short technical note on the quantization and ops guardrails you asked about:

- Recommended models: for your workload (short interactive analytics queries with occasional long context), we recommend the 13B and 70B families we demoed with our Redwood-optimized int4 kernels.
- Quality checks: we run a model-quality-eval (MQE) sweep with your prompt set (we ask for 50–100 representative prompts) and compute automated metrics plus 5 human evaluations for critical intents. If delta > 3% on key metrics, we revert quantization or apply mixed-precision fallback for the failing intents.
- Ops playbook: during pilot we instrument token-level traces and add three automated gates — latency SLO, generation divergence, and hallucination metric alerting. We can ship a playbook for your on-call/CS ops in the advisory engagement.

Performance numbers from internal benchmarks (representative):
- Baseline FP16: cost = 1.0x, P95 = 140ms
- Redwood int4 path: cost = 0.6x, P95 = 155ms (+15ms)
- Mixed fallback (hot spans): cost = 0.75x, P95 = 150ms

We’ll include a short table in the attached PDF to make this easier to compare.

-Karthik
Lead, Inference Optimizations
